sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK A. Readback and Hearback

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, taxi straight ahead, caution jet blast.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Oakport via the KEVNA TWO departure, BARSO transition, climb to 5,000 feet, squawk 3471.
WYNTA

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, climb to flight level 310, cross WYNTA at 220 knots or less.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 3,000 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway 15 approach.

sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK B. Checking, Clarifying, Confirming, Informing

body.text: Your required takeoff distance today is 2,100 metres. Ground has told you that an intersection departure from Golf 4 leaves 2,400 metres available. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him what distance you need.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, are you able to accept an intersection departure from Golf 4?
Approach first told you to maintain 7,000 feet. A few minutes later the same controller cleared you down to 5,000 feet, and you are level at 5,000 now. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, confirm maintaining 7,000 feet?

While in the cruise you saw what looked like a drone, about 2 miles away at your ten o'clock and slightly below. You were dealing with a level change and did not report it. Now ATC contacts you. Acknowledge the instruction, and report what you saw.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Fenwick Control, radar contact, maintain flight level 330.
Your RNAV equipment is inoperative today and the aircraft is dispatched under the minimum equipment list. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him what you need instead.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, expect the RNAV runway 15 approach.
Approach told you to contact the next controller on 128.3. You set 128.5 by mistake and heard nothing, so you have come back to the previous frequency. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, I have been calling you. Say the frequency you were given.
Marchfield Approach / WYNTA / expected further clearance

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK A. Role-play & Follow-up

pre.text: Flight Paths In this scenario, you'll be the pilot flying HL123, which goes through 2 flight stages: Descent, Approach.
Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, level at flight level 290 and 90 miles from DORLIN, inbound to Marchfield Airport. You have 1 hour 5 minutes of fuel on board.

body.text: Contact Fenwick Control, report your position and request descent.
DORLIN ONE arrival / ILS runway 15
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Fenwick Control, descend to flight level 190, reduce speed to 280 knots, expect the DORLIN ONE arrival, ILS runway 15, Marchfield altimeter 30.12.
DORLIN / Oakport
Listen to the controller and respond accordingly. Tell him what you need to know before you decide.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Marchfield Approach, they're clearing snow off runway 15 — it'll be about 15 minutes. You can hold at DORLIN or go to Oakport, it's 30 minutes from you. Up to you.
Listen to the controller, state your decision with a reason, and tell him how much fuel you have.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, once they're done it'll be about 10 more minutes to touchdown from the hold.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger, hold at DORLIN, right turns, maintain flight level 190, expect further clearance at one five.

pre.text: Situation Update The snow clearing is finished and you are leaving the hold.

body.text: Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, runway 15 is open, descend to 5,000 feet, turn left heading 120 for vectors to the ILS.

pre.text: Situation Update You are established on the ILS for runway 15 and passing 2,200 feet.

body.text: Contact Marchfield Tower, report your position and intention.
Listen to the tower, give a full readback, and tell him whether you can do that.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, Marchfield Tower, wind 150 at 12, runway 15, cleared to land. Vacate via Delta if you can, the A319 behind you is tight.
stand 24 / Delta / Mike
Listen to the ground controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, Marchfield Ground, taxi to stand 24 via Delta and Mike, give way to the King Air coming out of stand 22.
Listen to the ground controller, state your decision with a reason, and make any request you need.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, I'm sorry about that — stand 24 is still occupied. I can give you stand 31, but it's a long taxi, another 8 minutes. What would you like?
You have just finished Task A, as the pilot of Hotel Lima one two three.

In this situation, Approach offered you a hold at DORLIN or a diversion to Oakport while they cleared the snow. What did you need to know before you decided, and why? In your role as a pilot, how do you decide whether to hold or divert? Give an example of a situation where you would divert straight away rather than hold.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK B. Extended Role-play : Single Incident/Emergency Related

pre.text: Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, level at flight level 240 and 80 miles from BARSO, inbound to Oakport Airport. You have information Romeo.

body.text: Contact Oakport Approach and report your position.
BARSO ONE arrival / ILS runway 27
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Oakport Approach, descend to 10,000 feet, reduce speed to 250 knots, expect the BARSO ONE arrival, ILS runway 27, Oakport altimeter 29.88.

pre.text: Situation Update Passing 15,000 feet you fly through a flock of birds. Engine number 2 starts vibrating heavily. You have reduced thrust on that engine and the vibration has settled, but you must keep the speed at 230 knots or less and you cannot use full thrust on it. There is no fire and the engine is still running.

body.text: Inform the controller of your situation, tell him what you have done about it, and request priority for landing.
Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him both speeds.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger. For spacing with the traffic ahead I need 210 knots or less. Can you do that?
Listen to the controller, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, thank you. Turn left heading 300 for vectors to the ILS, descend to 6,000 feet. Say your intentions.
Listen to the controller and provide both pieces of information.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, two things — do you want the fire service, and will you need to shut that engine down before landing?

pre.text: Situation Update The vibration has dropped further and engine number 2 is now running normally at reduced thrust.

body.text: Listen to the controller, then state your decision with a reason.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the wind has backed — runway 09 now has a 10 knot headwind instead of a tailwind on 27. Do you want to change?
Contact the controller, give him an update on the engine, and say what you will need on arrival.
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 2,000 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway 09 approach, contact Oakport Tower on 120.9.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK C. Reporting about Task B

pre.text: Now listen to the controller's radiotelephony messages.

pre.label: ATC
pre.text: HL123, Oakport Approach, descend to 10,000 feet, reduce speed to 250 knots, expect the BARSO ONE arrival, ILS runway 27, Oakport altimeter 29.88.

pre.label: ATC
pre.text: HL123, roger. For spacing with the traffic ahead I need 210 knots or less. Can you do that?

pre.label: ATC
pre.text: HL123, thank you. Turn left heading 300 for vectors to the ILS, descend to 6,000 feet. Say your intentions.

pre.label: ATC
pre.text: HL123, two things — do you want the fire service, and will you need to shut that engine down before landing?

pre.label: ATC
pre.text: HL123, the wind has backed — runway 09 now has a 10 knot headwind instead of a tailwind on 27. Do you want to change?

pre.label: ATC
pre.text: HL123, descend to 2,000 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway 09 approach, contact Oakport Tower on 120.9.

body.text: What happened to your aircraft (HL123)? Explain the nature of the incident.
How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
